name: Habib Wahid

global_influences.artist_or_genre: Karsh Kale / British-Asian electronic music scene
global_influences.evidence: While studying audio engineering in the UK, Habib Wahid worked with Asian-fusion producers such as Karsh Kale, directly shaping his approach to blending electronic/urban production techniques with South Asian folk material.

Wahid's signature style fuses traditional Baul/Lalon folk elements with modern techno, urban beats, and pop-electronic production, a direct adaptation of Western/global electronic dance music techniques to Bangla folk source material.
global_influences.source: Wikipedia Habib Wahid; Putumayo artist profile

local_adaptation_notes: As the son of pop artist Ferdous Wahid, Habib Wahid built on a family pop lineage while pioneering a specifically Bangladeshi fusion genre: traditional Baul and Lalon folk vocal/melodic material re-rendered through electronic production, EDM textures and urban pop-beat arrangements. This made him a pivotal figure in shifting Bangladeshi pop away from purely band-based rock/pop toward producer-driven, studio-centric electronic-folk fusion.
sound_evolution_summary: Breakthrough period (2003): debut album Krishno introduced his folk-electronic fusion approach and produced an instant hit title track. Consolidation period (2005–2008): Moina Go and Shono extended the fusion sound and established him as a leading pop producer-artist. Later period: continued work as composer/producer across films and singles, including award-winning film scoring (Bangladesh National Film Award for Best Music Director, Projapoti, 2011), reflecting a shift toward broader production/composition work beyond solo albums.
concert_culture_notes: Primarily a studio/production-centered artist; public visibility driven more by radio, television, and streaming hits and film soundtrack work than by a dedicated touring band circuit, distinguishing his career pattern from guitar-band acts like LRB or Miles.
listener_community_notes: Represents a pivotal node bridging traditional folk/Baul listener communities and younger, urban pop/electronic audiences; frequently referenced as a key figure in the Pop genre's global-influence column (contemporary pop, R&B, electronic pop) within the BMEM framework.
